result.summary: Not ready to implement: manifest replay can bypass the proposed quarantine protection.

findings.title: Protect quarantine paths during manifest replay too
findings.body: Y6 promises immunity to forged manifest entries, but the spec requires reverse() to remain unchanged. Its file handler accepts {kind:'file', path:'<state>/quarantine/<name>'} without a hash and deletes that target because it is inside the allowed core. If the shelf is empty at the gate and a concurrent dream preserves that filename before replay, reverse() destroys the new copy before the protected disposer runs. The manifest can remain unchanged throughout, so the byte-comparison guard does not help. An in-memory probe of the actual reverse() confirmed this entry passes validation and invokes rmSync.
findings.recommendation: Permit and require a quarantine guard in reverse() before mutating dispatch, covering shelf paths and resolved aliases. Add an interleaving test with a pre-existing forged entry, an empty initial inventory, and a preserve completed before replay; assert the original bytes survive.

next_steps: Extend the preservation contract and acceptance tests to cover manifest replay before dispatch.
